title: Service account rotation & access journey — UX sketch notes
content:
Context: quick UX exploration for org/team settings around long-lived credentials (service accounts + API keys), rotation, and lightweight audit surfaces. Goal is a low-friction flow that encourages regular key rotation, makes risk visible to org admins, and plays nicely with RBAC (team-level vs org-level).

This is a working sketch — lots of open questions and TODOs. Not intended as final mocks. Focus areas: discoverability, bulk operations for large orgs, and simple recovery/fallback story.

Top-level flows to support (user stories):
- As an org admin, I want to see all active service accounts and keys across teams, filter by last-rotated / last-used, so I can schedule rotation and revoke stale keys.
- As a team owner, I want to rotate a service account key with zero-downtime option (create new key, deploy, then revoke old) and see recommended rotation interval based on usage.
- As a developer, I want to create a short-lived API key for ephemeral CI job and auto-expire it after 24h.
- As a security reviewer, I want to quickly audit which keys were used to access production models in the last 30 days.

Wireframe notes (desktop first):
1) Console > Settings > Security / Access > Credentials Overview (landing):
   - Header: "Credentials & Service Accounts" small description: show counts (service accounts, active keys, expiring keys).
   - Main table (paginated, server-side): columns: Name | Owner (team) | Type (service account / api-key) | Last used | Last rotated | Status | Actions
   - Quick filters (chips): Expiring in 7 days, Never used, Unrotated (>=90d), Owned by external contractor, Team: <dropdown>.
   - Row actions: Rotate key (opens slide-over), Create short-lived key, Revoke, View audit trail (small modal). Bulk checkbox for multi-select + bulk revoke / mark-for-rotation.

   UX decisions: Default sort = Last used desc. But add saved views: "Security triage" (show never used + unrotated) and "Operational" (active by last use).

2) Rotate key slide-over (mobile-friendly):
   - Step 1: Create replacement key (auto-generate). Option: TTL (1h, 24h, 7d, custom). Checkbox: "Allow overlap window" with slider for overlap minutes (default 15m).
   - Step 2: Deploy instructions (copy key, or download .json). Inline tips: "Use env var: REDWOOD_SA_KEY=..." plus link to SDK quickstart.
   - Step 3: Revoke old key (disabled until user confirms successful deploy OR until chosen delay has passed).

   Edge cases noted: If key is used in scheduled jobs without proper propagation, overlap window must be configurable per org policy. Add a warning when rotation affects Dedicated clusters (longer propagation).

3) Service account detail page:
   - Top: name, description, team(s) allowed to impersonate, created_by, creation_date, last_activity.
   - Right rail: Quick actions: create key, rotate, set ttl default, set approvers.
   - Middle: keys list (compact): key id, created_at, last_used, expires_at, status, fingerprint, environment tags. Each key row: "download" (only once at creation), "revoke" (with confirm), "mark as compromised" (triggers org notification flow).
   - Below: "Who has access" — RBAC mapping with small graph: Org -> Teams -> Principals. Click a team to open membership and rule that grants access.

4) Audit view (lightweight):
   - Filtered by object type (service-account-key, api-key), principal, route, model id, date range.
   - Helpful quick filters: failed auth attempts, keys created outside of SSO-managed flows, keys used from new IP address.
   - Entries are searchable and show contextual popover: "Key X used to call model gpt-8-prod -> 2025-11-02 14:05 UTC, tokens: 3.2k".

Design patterns & microcopy:
- Use microcopy to reduce fear: "Revoke is non-destructive to model artifacts; it only prevents this key from calling the runtime."
- Explain overlap: "Overlap window lets you create a replacement key and keep the old one active for a short period while you update deployments. Recommended: 15–30 minutes for ephemeral infra, 24h for scheduled jobs."
- On download screen: emphasize that the secret is shown once. Provide 'staging-only' suggestion for testing.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- List + filters of credentials with working bulk revoke + rotate slide-over (functional, no animation).
- Rotate flow must produce a new key and allow scheduled revoke of old key with configurable delay.
- Audit view filters by key id and principal and shows last 90 days of events.
- RBAC mappings visible on service account page (read-only for non-admins).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Where does API key creation live? Under "Service accounts" or "API keys" top-level? Pros: centralizing simplifies discovery. Cons: mixing long-lived service account keys vs short-term API keys might confuse. Suggest two tabs on the landing page.
- Do we enforce organ-wide rotation policies (e.g., 90d) or surface recommendations? Enforcement requires org policy engine change; for MVP we surface warnings and a "policy status" column.
- Should key 'last used' be approximate to avoid privacy/PII? We need legal input (CONF-3389).

Operational notes (engineering impacts):
- Backend: API to create key with TTL and overlap window; endpoints to schedule revoke at T+window; events sent to audit stream with structured fields (key_id, sa_id, principal, model_id, tokens). Ticket: PROD-4821.
- Telemetry: Add metric for "time-to-rotate" per team (to prioritize nudges).
- SRE: When revoking, ensure cache invalidation of KV caches that may still hold auth zustand; verify propagation timings for Dedicated and Private installs.

Proposed rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (internal): MVP list + rotate slide-over + audit filters (beta) — open to customers as opt-in.
- Phase 2: Org policy enforcement, bulk rotation scheduling, automated emails to owners when key nearing expiry.
- Phase 3: Integrations: Github Actions secret rotation template, Terraform provider support.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add mock CSV export for bulk compliance teams.
- Coordinate with legal on last-used reporting (CONF-3389).
- Check with infra about ability to create short-lived keys with TTL=1h (Ava).
- UX: create low-fidelity screens for mobile narrow width (Jordan).
- Schedule review w/ security 2025-12-15.

Sketch (ASCII quick):
[Credentials & Service Accounts]  Search | Filter chips | + New credential
-----------------------------------------------------------
| Checkbox | Name | Team | Type | Last used | Last rotated | Status | Actions |
-----------------------------------------------------------
| [ ] | analytics-sa | Data | SA-key | 2025-11-30 | 2025-09-01 | Active | Rotate / Revoke / Audit |

Quick flow notes: choose 'Rotate' -> slide-over -> generate key -> copy & deploy -> optional auto-revoke in 1h -> confirm.

Questions for next sync:
- Should we surface "risk score" per key (unused + high-privilege => high risk)? If yes, compute on backend and show a 1-5 badge.
- Bulk rotation: do we allow a single action to rotate many keys at once (creates N new keys)? Probably not — better to mark for rotation and create scheduled job per key.

Relevant tickets / PRs: PROD-4821 (rotation API), PR 214 (frontend slide-over), CONF-3389 (legal), UX-762 (mobile sketches).

End of draft.
